blocks.markdown: Every Spanish word has one stressed syllable. A written accent (*tilde*) marks it when the usual rules would put the stress elsewhere: *can-**ción***, *te-**lé**-fo-no*. Without a tilde, words ending in a vowel, *n* or *s* stress the second-to-last syllable: *ca-**mi**-no*.

blocks.hint: A tilde, if there is one, sits on the stressed syllable.
blocks.solution_explanation: The tilde marks the stress; without one, the ending decides.

blocks.prompt: Tap every verb in the sentence.

items.text: Yo como pan y bebo agua.
Ella lee un libro y escucha música.

blocks.solution_explanation: *como* and *bebo* (or *lee* and *escucha*) are what the person does.

blocks.prompt: Tap the letter that English does not have.
blocks.solution_explanation: **ñ** is a letter of its own in Spanish.
